Shipley issued the following directive, MARADMIN 550/19, outlining the guidelines for activating and deactivating Reserve Component (RC) Marines who are ordered to active duty in support of defense operations during civil emergencies in the United States.

👉the following is a complete summary of this standing order, which you can sauce here: https://www.marines.mil/News/Messages/Messages-Display/Article/1979422/manpower-guidance-for-activation-and-deactivation-of-reserve-component-marines/

--------------

MANPOWER GUIDANCE FOR ACTIVATION AND DEACTIVATION OF RESERVE COMPONENT MARINES ORDERED TO ACTIVE DUTY ISO DEFENSE SUPPORT OF CIVIL AUTHORITIES | Date Signed: 10/3/2019 | MARADMINS Number: 550/19

--------------

1. Purpose: The MARADMIN aims to cancel the previous MARADMIN 300/14 and provide guidance for activating RC Marines under Title 10, U.S. Code, Section 12304a, following a request for federal assistance in response to a major disaster or emergency within the United States.

2. Background: a. If a Governor requests federal assistance for a disaster or emergency, the Secretary of Defense may order Marine Corps Reserve units to active duty for up to 120 days without the member's consent. b. Activation authority for Section 12304a is delegated to the Secretary of the Navy (SECNAV) by the Secretary of Defense. c. Immediate Response Authority is granted to Commanders to save lives or prevent property damage.

3. Process: a. The activation process involves identifying Selected Marine Corps Reserve (SMCR) units, preparing activation packages, submitting orders to the Joint Staff, and activating designated units via naval message. b. Marine Emergency Preparedness Liaison Officers (EPLO) are activated in coordination with U.S. Northern Command (USNORTHCOM) and U.S. Indo-Pacific Command (USINDOPACOM). c. Individual Augments (IA) are sourced from the Individual Ready Reserve (IRR) or Individual Mobilization Augmentee (IMA) program.

4. Actions: a. Various Marine Corps entities, such as Deputy Commandant Plans, Policies, and Operations (DC PPO) and Deputy Commandant Manpower and Reserve Affairs (DC MRA), are involved in coordinating, funding, and activating units. b. Commands are responsible for activating units and individuals, submitting requests, authenticating orders, and providing reporting instructions. c. Operational Sponsors submit activation requests and provide reporting instructions. 

5. Coordinating Instructions: a. Mobilization-to-dwell ratios are not considered for Section 12304a activations. b. Marines pending mandatory retirement will retire as scheduled, and those pending involuntary separations will not be activated. c. Enlisted members without an end-of-contract date covering the contingency period will not be activated. d. Leave, travel, and other entitlements are specified based on the duration of activation.

6. MCTFS Actions: Instructions are provided for reporting and updating Marine Corps Total Force System (MCTFS) for members mobilized for different periods, including reporting codes and entitlements.

7. Entitlements: Details are provided regarding entitlements for Marines on orders lasting 1-30 days and 31-120 days, covering housing, allowances, leave, and other benefits.

8. Additional Instructions: a. Accrued leave, fitness reports, and proficiency/conduct marks are administered following specific regulations. b. Line of duty investigations for injuries and procedures for legal hold orders are outlined. c. Specific guidance for contingencies, including reporting instructions and crisis event codes, will be released separately.

9. Applicability: The message is applicable to the entire Marine Corps Total Force.

--------------

10. Release Authority: The message is released by Brigadier General Daniel L. Shipley, Director, Manpower Plans and Policy.
